summary: Columbus County steel tower, 100 ft, completed 1931 about a mile east of Chadbourn; no source found says whether it still stands.

facts.design: Steel tower with an enclosed cab and an inside stairway
facts.agency: North Carolina Division of Forest Resources

events.note: Completion reported August 1931: a 100-foot steel tower about one mile east of Chadbourn on State Highway 20

evidence.supports: 1930 announcement of a lookout for western Columbus County, from the state Department of Conservation and Development
evidence.quote: it was announced yesterday at the Department of Conservation and Development

evidence.supports: Planned 100-foot steel tower with an inside stairway
evidence.quote: The structure will be of steel construction, 100 feet in height and will have an inside stairway.

evidence.supports: Planned enclosed cab at the top
evidence.quote: A station for a fire lookout will be in an enclosed cabin at the top of the shaft.

evidence.supports: Planned view of about 15 miles in every direction
evidence.quote: The lookout will have a range of vision of about 15 miles radius in all directions.

evidence.supports: May 1930 notice: site probably about two miles east of town
evidence.quote: the tower will probably be placed about two miles east of Chadbourn

evidence.supports: August 1931: completed, 100-foot steel tower one mile east of Chadbourn near State Highway 20
evidence.quote: The erection of a 100-foot high steel forest fire observation tower near state highway number twenty, one mile east of Chadbourn has been completed.

evidence.supports: Tower called the 22nd unit in a proposed statewide system of 125
evidence.quote: It is the 22nd unit in a proposed state-wide system of 125.

evidence.supports: September 1931: about one mile east of Chadbourn on State Highway No. 20
evidence.quote: about 1 mile east of Chadbourn on State Highway No. 20

evidence.supports: Site land given to the state by C. R. Bailey of Chadbourn

evidence.supports: Columbus County tower listed under the North Carolina Division of Forest Resources

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The May 1930 announcement said the site would probably be about two miles east of Chadbourn; the August and September 1931 completion notices say about one mile east on State Highway 20. The story follows the 1931 notices.

sources.title: North Carolina fire tower list (NCT030 Chadbourn)

notes_for_editor: Two records describe this tower. us-nc-chadbourn (Eastern US Lookouts) gives 34.3248, -78.8084, 30.5 m and the NC Division of Forest Resources; this record gives 34.27916, -78.81527 from the tnlandforms list. The two points are about 5.1 km apart. They may be the same 1931 tower, so a human should decide whether to merge them. The cab and stairway come from the 1930 plan; the 1931 notices do not repeat those details. The 30.5 m height is the 100-foot figure from the sources; no source gives the cab-floor height. A search snippet mentioned an 80-foot Chadbourn tower built in 1928; no page I read says that, and it conflicts with these notices, so it is not used. No source after 1931 was found, so status, access and what remains today are unknown. Fact-check 2026-10-21: the cited tnlandforms.us page does not name Tom Dunigan, so that name was removed from the story and this record; restore it only from a source that names him. The 13 May 1930 and 4 August 1931 dates were confirmed on the Forest Lookouts page.
